title: GATEWAY_CONFIG
description: The JSON object in the GATEWAY_CONFIG variable of Jean's gateway (gateway/gateway.js, D191), which relays to the services a browser can't reach. It holds the apps' secrets: keep it in the environment, never in a file Jean's folder serves.

$schema.description: This schema's address, for an editor; the gateway doesn't read it

origins.description: The addresses Jean is served from, as origins: the only pages the gateway answers with CORS

hosts.description: The hosts it relays to, over HTTPS (or HTTP on this computer); a name covers its subdomains. An origin over plain HTTP, named whole, is relayed to as well, such as an authority's OCSP responder. Left out: those of every service Jean knows that a browser can't reach, their sign-ins included

clients.description: Apps registered with sign-in servers that take only apps they know: Jean signs in with the client id, and the gateway adds the secret where the code is traded for tokens, so the secret never reaches a browser

timestamps.description: RFC 3161 services that date Jean's certificates and that a browser can't reach, such as a qualified one (D276): relayed to and announced

logs.description: Public logs, such as Sigstore's Rekor, certificates may be recorded in (D276): relayed to and announced

issuer.description: The sign-in server's issuer, as its metadata names it

tokenEndpoint.description: Where the code is traded for tokens: the only address the secret goes to

clientId.description: The app's client id, which Jean signs in with

auth.description: How the secret goes: in the form (client_secret_post) or as HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic)
